subject: Proposal: Dedicated GPU increase + autoscale SLA amendment
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma.li@fintechiq.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@fintechiq.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — need reserved GPUs + autoscale changes

Hi Karthik,

We’re starting renewal discussions for FinTech IQ and want to expand our Dedicated footprint as part of the new term. Current summary: we’re on a 6x A10G reserved pool (regional: us-west) with frequent bursts during end-of-month processing windows. In the last six weeks peak sustained throughput hit ~420 rps for text-generation endpoints and token throughput peaks at ~10k tokens/sec.

Requests for renewal amendment:
- Add +8 A10G reserved GPUs to the pool (to be available immediately at renewal).
- Add a warm pool sized to 2x replica warm images to reduce cold-starts during batch runs.
- Formalize an hourly throughput target during business hours (8am–8pm PT) of 350 rps sustained with 99.5% availability.
- Shorter scale-up lag during scheduled month-end windows (target < 45s to full capacity).

Can you confirm feasibility and provide pricing delta and any operational caveats? I’ve attached a simple capacity plan with our observed traffic patterns. Procurement will want the SLA language and a sample amendment for legal review.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Head of Platform Engineering
FinTech IQ

Attachments: FinTechIQ_capacity-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma.li@fintechiq.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — need reserved GPUs + autoscale changes

Emma — thanks for the detail and the attachment, that helps a lot. Looping in Marissa (AM) and Jordan (SE) to scope the technical and commercial pieces. High-level response below and a proposed path to finalize during the renewal: 

Summary feasibility: yes, we can provision +8 A10G to the Dedicated pool at renewal and create a warm pool. We can also commit to a throughput target with a supported operational SLA, but the exact SLA language and the compensations are tied to committed reserved capacity and monitoring windows.

Proposed autoscale/amendment items (initial):
- Reserved pool increase: +8 A10G (makes pool total 14 A10G dedicated in us-west).
- Autoscale policy: min_replicas = 4, max_replicas = 16; warm_pool = 2 dedicated prewarmed replicas; scale_up_target = 60s standard, with a guaranteed scale_up_lag <= 45s for scheduled windows (month-end maintenance window to be prebooked).
- Throughput guarantee: 350 rps sustained (8am–8pm PT) with 99.5% uptime measured at the model-route level; exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force-majeure as usual.
- Costing model: incremental reserved GPU fee + monthly warm pool fee (flat per replica), plus a small premium for 45s guaranteed scale-up SLAs during scheduled windows. I’ll attach a proposed amendment that maps these items to line-item pricing.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Jordan to provide a short technical note on how we implement the warm pool and how we validate the 45s scale-up latency (load-testing plan).
2) Marissa to provide pricing delta and a redline for the amendment.
3) Quick call this week (30 minutes) to lock scope and get procurement comfortable.

Jordan/Marissa — Emma’s team is sensitive to month-end latency, so please prioritize the scale-up guarantees and the measurement method. Emma — what month-end dates are critical for you (first closing month-end of the renewed term)?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager — Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-amendment-dedicated.pdf (draft amendment)

Subject: Technical note: warm pool and scale-up validation plan

Emma / team — quick technical note on how we would implement and validate the requested autoscale changes.

Implementation details:
- Warm pool behavior: we’ll maintain 2 warm replicas per region for the reserved pool. Warm replicas keep the model and runtime primed (KV cache warm, model shards loaded) and accept traffic immediately. They are billed as warm_pool instances and do not consume burstable capacity.
- Autoscaler params (recommended): min_replicas = 4; target_cpu_utilization = 55%; target_latency_p50 = 40ms; max_replicas = 16.
- Scale-up mechanics: normal scale-up relies on container startup + model load; to hit the <45s target we’ll use pre-pulled images and a fast-start kernel path for your month-end windows. That reduces kernel selection time and model shard warm-time.
- Measurement: we measure scale_up_lag as the window between an autoscaler trigger (queue length > threshold) to the first steady-state replica accepting traffic above 85% of target throughput. We’ll publish both raw traces and aggregated 5m window metrics to your console.

Validation / test plan:
1) Staging load test: synthetic ramp to 500 rps with the proposed autoscaler settings to verify steady-state and scale-up behavior.
2) Warm-pool stress: cycle warm replicas offline and validate warm replacement time under 5s for image attach and <45s for traffic-ready.
3) Production pilot: run a one-week pilot during a non-critical month-end with increased monitoring and a rollback runbook.

I’ve posted the load-testing plan and scripts here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/load-testing-plan

If this looks OK I’ll schedule the staging runs and a short walkthrough for your infra team.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
